description: DO NOT REMOVE 'Bash(bash *)' FROM THIS FILE'S DENY LIST. Doing so does not activate the 'Bash(bash bootstrap/query_issues.sh *)' allow below — it is currently INERT (see why below) — it instead reopens a CRITICAL exploit verified live against the shipped 2.1.272 CLI (security-reviewer; escalated to architect as #1678: 'a prefix-matched Bash allowlist grants arbitrary code execution via argument injection; postures are either exploitable or inert'). Evidence: with that deny entry removed, a command matching the allowed bootstrap/query_issues.sh prefix but carrying a nested 'bash -c "..."' payload (via ';' chaining or $(...) substitution) executed with zero permission denials; restoring the deny entry blocks it (verified DENIED, permission_denials populated, no file written). Why the allow is inert regardless: this CLI's own permission-decision code (checkRuleBasedPermissions/GB rule-matching path, read directly from ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.272) checks matching deny rules before allow rules at every match tier and returns on the first deny hit without ever consulting the allow set — no specificity exception for a more specific allow. So as long as 'Bash(bash *)' sits in this deny list, the narrower allow below grants nothing; removing the deny does not fix that, it only removes the one thing that was blocking the exploit above. Fixing this properly (delivering bash-based gh-read without the injection surface) is an open architectural decision, tracked as #1678 — candidates include a fixed-argv wrapper, a PreToolUse hook rejecting shell metacharacters, or dropping bash-based grants from postures entirely; none chosen, none built here. Separately, and not a mitigation for any of the above: this CLI also auto-approves a distinct class of commands it judges safe (e.g. plain reads) regardless of an allow list's narrowness and regardless of --permission-mode manual — that class does not include a nested 'bash -c' invocation, which is exactly what the exploit above used. Until #1678 is resolved, this posture provides read-only filesystem + local shell exactly like review-read-only and nothing more; the query_issues.sh read path is not yet functional.
